header:
Date: 2026-09-16
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Ellen Ruiz (SummitCare Dir ML Ops), Tom Becker (CTO), Priya Sharma (SRE), Luis Ortega (Platform Eng)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review load-test results vs incumbent provider. Redwood showed better median latency and higher sustained throughput under load; customer raised concerns about tail latency, cold-starts, and private network integration. Agreed next steps: share raw artifacts, run KV-cache cold-start test, and customer to decide on Dedicated slot trial.
topics: Load test summary and spot checks
Next steps: Dedicated slot decision and follow-up tests
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Ellen Ruiz: Ellen here. Tom's on. Priya, Luis.
[00:10] Tom Becker: Hey.
[00:12] Maya Chen: Maya from Redwood, hi all.
[00:15] Jordan Patel: Cool. Agenda — we ran the 30-minute load soak yesterday, we'll walk through p50/p90/p99, throughput numbers, then talk tail and cold starts and next steps.
[01:05] Ellen Ruiz: Sounds good. We looked at the summary you sent but wanted to talk through a few spikes we saw in the evening run.
[01:22] Maya Chen: Right, so quick top line: in our test harness with the model you agreed (40B variant, quantized), Redwood median generation latency was ~120ms for the 256 token prompt path, p90 at 240ms, p99 at 580ms. IncumbentVendor's numbers from your baseline spreadsheet were p50 210ms, p90 430ms, p99 1.1s — so we see about ~40–45% improvement at median and roughly half the tail.
[02:05] Priya Sharma: Those are promising but our SLO is p95 < 300ms for interactive parts. p99 is concerning because we have a handful of UX flows that can't tolerate spikes.
[02:18] Jordan Patel: Totally, that's why we instrumented the KV cache tests — a lot of tail is from cache misses and cold KV instantiation when concurrent sessions spike. We also logged scheduling jitter in one run — that marginally increased p99.
[02:52] Luis Ortega: Can you say more about the cache miss behavior? We saw a gap at minute 22 where latency doubled.
[03:03] Maya Chen: Yeah that was during the synthetic warm-up drop. We flush the in-memory prefixes during the bucket rotation in our harness to simulate hundreds of unique sessions; the incidence of cache misses rose. When we pinned a 4-hour steady state, p99 dropped to ~480ms. So steady state is better than short spike behavior.
[03:44] Tom Becker: What's the throughput? We need sustained RPS for peak clinic hours — roughly 450 RPS with 75 concurrency.
[03:51] Maya Chen: In the orchestrated run, Redwood sustained 520 RPS at the target request size (average 240 tokens generated) with 20% headroom, CPU/GPU utilization in the cluster at ~78%. IncumbentVendor sustained 330 RPS under same conditions.
[04:15] Ellen Ruiz: Are those numbers for Hosted API or Dedicated?
[04:19] Maya Chen: Those are on the Redwood dedicated test pool we provisioned for the POC (dedicated GPUs but in our testing env). On Hosted the p50 was slightly higher (~140ms) but within the same ballpark; throughput dropped about 8%.
[04:40] Priya Sharma: Firewall and VPC — we attempted to send logs to your collector yesterday and the connection timed out for a subset of IPs. Any specifics?
[04:50] Jordan Patel: We saw that — looks like an egress rule on your side blocked the collector range. We'll send the IP list and port ranges; Maya will confirm the collector scaling too.
[05:06] Maya Chen: I'll also share a quick script to validate connectivity.
[05:12] Ellen Ruiz: Good. On security: do you have SOC2 Type II and KMS/HSM options in Private?
[05:20] Jordan Patel: Yes, Redwood Private supports KMS integrations and we can engage our compliance team for SOC2 artifacts; we already sent the SOC2 summary in the doc pack but we can provide the full report under NDA.
[05:34] Tom Becker: Cost side: Redwood shows higher throughput, but what's the expected cost per 1M tokens vs our incumbent? Our procurement will want numbers.
[05:43] Maya Chen: Early estimate from Optimize tooling: for this workload Redwood would be ~12% lower unit cost at steady state considering fewer retries and better batching. We will send a cost model spreadsheet showing assumptions.
[06:02] Priya Sharma: Can you explain batching behavior? We saw some variance in latency when batch size changed.
[06:10] Maya Chen: The runtime does continuous batching; latency is influenced by target latency SLO and batch accumulation window. For low-latency SLOs we run smaller batches — increases compute overhead but keeps p50 low. For higher throughput we open the window slightly longer. We'll share the config we used for the tests (batching window 8ms, max batch 64).
[06:42] Ellen Ruiz: Any plan for quantization — we ran 4-bit on the incumbent with quality drop. How'd Redwood handle 4-bit?
[06:49] Maya Chen: We ran a simulated int4 quant run. Quality delta was negligible on your eval set (BLEU-style proxy drop <0.5%). Performance improved: p50 down to 95ms, p90 180ms. We flagged a couple of edge cases where hallucination risk rose, we'll annotate those prompts in the shared spreadsheet.
[07:18] Tom Becker: Tail behavior after warm-up — is there an autoscaling quirk? We saw a brief window where additional nodes spun up and latency spiked.
[07:27] Jordan Patel: That's expected during horizontal scaling events. We can smooth that with pre-warmed spare slots or guaranteed Dedicated capacity. If you want predictable latency, Dedicated slots remove that autoscaling variance.
[08:00] Priya Sharma: How much Dedicated capacity would we need to cover 99% of peaks?
[08:05] Maya Chen: Based on your 450 RPS peak and observed per-GPU throughput, we'd recommend 6x mid-range A100-equivalent slots to have headroom and linear failure tolerance. We can refine with the exact instance sizing if you want a cost estimate.
[08:28] Luis Ortega: Any requirements on network peering for Private? We need to keep data in-region.
[08:34] Jordan Patel: Private supports VPC peering and on-prem connectors; we can pin region and also support HSM/KMS key residency to meet data residency rules.
[08:50] Ellen Ruiz: Back to the anomalies — there were ~12 events where p99 jumped beyond 1s during the evening run. Do you have stack traces or logs?
[08:58] Maya Chen: We captured request IDs. We saw two causes: transient disk-backed KV fetch under pressure and a scheduling jitter aligned with a GC event from the orchestration node. We'll hand over the request IDs and the raw logs.
[09:22] Tom Becker: If we run a Dedicated slot trial, can we reproduce your exact harness in our infra? We want deterministic reproduction.
[09:30] Maya Chen: Yes — we'll provide the dockerized harness and the exact config (traffic profile, seeds) so you can run the same test. We recommend running an overnight 12-hour soak to capture diurnal patterns.
[09:48] Ellen Ruiz: Good. What about canary/fallback — if you roll a new model or config and tail spikes, do you have automatic fallback?
[09:57] Jordan Patel: We support rollouts with automatic fallback to previous model/variant and route-splitting for canary. Also metric gates tied to p99/p90 alerts so an automatic rollback can trigger if thresholds cross.
[10:18] Priya Sharma: One practical ask: can you annotate the spreadsheet with request IDs that correspond to each latency spike so we can cross-ref?
[10:25] Maya Chen: Yes, will do. We'll also include the Grafana links with anchor points.
[10:33] Luis Ortega: From infra ops: what's the expected outbound connections for logs and telemetry? We need to document allowed CIDR/IPs.
[10:40] Jordan Patel: We'll send a table with IP ranges, ports, and TLS requirements; collector uses mutual TLS, and we support pulling via S3 ingestion if you prefer egress-free.
[10:55] Ellen Ruiz: That S3 ingestion option is interesting — helps with compliance.
[11:00] Tom Becker: On decision criteria, Ellen — can you outline go/no-go?
[11:05] Ellen Ruiz: We're looking at: p95 < 300ms for interactive calls, sustained throughput >= 450 RPS, <=15% cost delta vs incumbent or better, and private connectivity & SOC2 docs in place. If Redwood meets those, we'll push procurement to try Dedicated.
[11:27] Jordan Patel: Great. Quick recap of deliverables: I'll send raw latency CSV and Grafana links; Maya will run KV cold-start bake and quant tests; Priya will validate connectivity; Ellen to confirm SLO threshold email.
[11:47] Priya Sharma: One more operational note — we'd like a playbook for incident onboarding.
[11:54] Jordan Patel: We'll share the runbook and escalation matrix.
[12:00] Ellen Ruiz: Okay that's it from me. Thanks.
[12:05] Tom Becker: Thanks everyone.
[12:08] Maya Chen: I'll follow up with links and the harness by end of day tomorrow.
[12:13] Jordan Patel: Thanks, meeting adjourned.

Notes: shared artifacts referenced — "SummitCare_load_results_0915.csv" (link in CRM), Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abcd1234/summitcare-poc, test harness repo: https://git.redwood.ai/summitcare/poc-harness."
